This appeal has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 09.12.2019 passed by learned Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No. 1, Farrukhabad in Session Trial No. 67 of 2015 (State Vs. Urmila and Dharmendra,
have been convicted and sentenced to two years rigorous imprisonment under Section 498-A I.P.C.
along with a fine of Rs. 5,000/- each and on failure to deposit the fine to undergo additional imprisonment of two months, life imprisonment under Section 304-B I.P.C. and two years rigorous imprisonment under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act along with a fine of Rs. 2,000/- each and Smt. sentences.text: 2. The prosecution case is that the first informant-Brahmanand lodged an F.I.R. dated 12.11.2014 at 8:00 a.m. alleging therein that he had solemnized marriage of his daughter namely Puja with the accused-appellant, Dharmendra three years ago by spending beyond his means, soon after the marriage the in-laws of his daughter used to make demand of a motorcycle.
Fifteen days ago his daughter was send by her husband and mother-in-law after committing cruelty with her for demand of motorcycle.
His daughter had a child of one and half year.

One day prior, i.e., 11.11.2014 at about 6:00 p.m. he received information that husband and mother-in-law of his daughter had killed his daughter along with his relatives, thereafter they set ablaze her after pouring kerosene oil upon her.

On this written report the F.I.R. came to be lodged as Case Crime No. 315 of 2014, under Sections 498A, 304-B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kampil, District Farrukhabad against Dharmendra (husband), Ravindra (brother of husband) and Smt. Urmila (mother-in-law) along with unknown relatives of the husband of the deceased.

3. After lodging of the F.I.R. the police came in motion and inquest was conducted and thereafter body of the deceased was sent for postmortem, wherein superficial burn injury was found all over the body of the deceased along with one contusion of 3.00 c.m. x 2.00 c.m. over the left elbow.
4.

After investigation, the police submitted charge sheet against the accused-appellants in the court,
whereupon the concerned Magistrate took cognizance and the case was committed to the Court of Sessions.

Charges were framed against the accused-appellants which were denied and they claimed to be tried.
5. Prosecution examined as many as seven prosecution witnesses, i.e., P.W.1-Brahmanand (informant/ father of the deceased), P.W.2-Diwari Lal, P.W.3-Smt. Kavita (wife of the informant),
P.W.4-Dr. Pradeep Singh who conducted the postmortem of the deceased, P.W.5-Anil Kumar Tiwari (Naib Tehsildar), P.W.6-Head Constable Suraj Pal Singh and P.W.7-Ashok Kumar Rawat (Circle Officer.
6.
The informant deposed as P.W.1- before the trial court and stated that deceased was his daughter.

He had solemnized marriage of his daughter on 24.04.2012 with Dharmendra according to his status and means, when her daughter went to her matrimonial house her husband was not satisfied with the dowry given at the time of marriage and he used to make demand of additional dowry in the form of motorcycle and on account of non fulfilment thereof he used to commit cruelty with her.
After some time of marriage the husband of his daughter expelled her and when his daughter came to her parental house she told him that his husband used to make demand of motorcycle but he could not fullfill the said demand on account of his financial condition and after convincing her daughter sent her to her matrimonial house.
On 11.11.2014 at about 6:00 p.m. he has been informed on mobile phone that husband and mother-in-law of his daughter had killed his daughter by setting ablaze her after pouring kerosene oil upon her.

When he along with other persons reached at the matrimonial house of his daughter husband of his daughter along with his other family members were not present and the burned dead body of the deceased was lying there.

On lodging of the F.I.R.
by him the police conducted inquest proceeding in presence of Naib Tehsildar, thereafter Smt. Urmila And Another vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75150811/
2 postmortem was conducted.

sentences.text: He had proved his signature on the written report and the inquest report.
In his cross-examination P.W.1 has stated that the time of marriage no demand of dowry was made by the in-laws of daughter.
Dharmendra had made demand of motorcycle from his daughter after about one or one and half year.
She was expelled out from her matrimonial house prior to 15-20 days of her killing.
He received informant of death of his daughter on mobile phone at about 6:00 p.m. and he reached the matrimonial house of his daughter at about 10:30 hours in the night.
7. P.W.2-Diwari Lal in his statement before the trial court has stated that on 12.11.2014 inquest report of the deceased was prepared wherein he proved his signature.
In his cross-examination P.W.2 has stated that he received informant of death of the deceased at about 6-7 hours in the evening.
When he along with other persons reached at the matrimonial house of the deceased there was no person present there and only burned dead body of the deceased was lying there.
8. P.W.3-Smt. Kavita in her statement before the trial court has stated that the deceased was her step daughter, her marriage was solemnized six years prior with Dharmendra.

On account of non fulfillment of demand of dowry the deceased has been done to death by her in-laws by setting ablaze her after pouring kerosene and the F.I.R. of the incident was lodged by her husband (P.W.1).

In her cross-examination P.W.3 has stated that it is wrong to say that the deceased caught fire while cooking food and they have lodged false F.I.R.
9.

P.W.4-Dr. Pradeep Singh who conducted the postmortem of the deceased, in his statement before the trial court stated that on 12.11.2014 he was on duty at postmortem house in Fatehgarh where the dead body was brought.

The body of the deceased was average built, her eyes and mouth were open,
pugilistic attitude was present and smell of kerosene oil was coming out.
The deceased sustained superficial deep burn injury, both the soles of feet were not burnt, her skin was peeling off in several places and had turned black and dried up from burning.
He had proved postmortem report (Ex.Ka.-3).
In his cross-examination P.W.4 has stated that postmortem of the deceased was conducted by him and Dr. Brajesh.
On the right elbow of the deceased there was a contusion of size 3.0 c.m. x 2.0 c.m. which may be sustained due to fall.
The cause of death of the deceased was found to be shock as a result of ante mortem burn.
10. P.W.5-Anil Kumar Tiwari is the Nayab Tehsildar, who has proved inquest report and other papers.
11. P.W.6-Suraj Pal Singh is the Head Constable, who had registered the F.I.R. and G.D. entry and has proved his signature thereupon.
12. P.W.7-Ashok Kumar Rawat is the Circle Officer, who had proved his signature on the charge sheet and other police papers.

In his cross-examination he has stated that no one had told him that deceased was burned by the accused persons and on the basis of statements of family members of the deceased he has submitted the charge sheet against the accused persons.
13. Statements of accused were recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. in which they denied the facts of incidence and alleged that statements of witnesses are wrong and they are not guilty.

During trial Smt. Urmila And Another vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75150811/
3 the accused in their statements recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. stated that they have been falsely implicated, the deceased was insisting on staying at her maternal home, so she set herself on fire and except this defence version no other oral or documentary evidence was produced by them.

sentences.text:
14. After hearing the prosecution and defence counsel, the learned Additional Sessions Judge vide judgment and order dated 09.12.2019, exonerated the accused-appellant, Dharmendra of the charges under Section 302 I.P.C. and convicted both the accused-apellants, Smt. Urmila and Dharmendra under Section 304-B I.P.C. and sentenced them to undergo life imprisonment; they have been further convicted under Section 498-A I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo two years'
rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Rs. 5,000/- and in case of default of payment of fine to undergo additional two months' imprisonment; further they have been convicted under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and sentenced to undergo two years rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Rs.
2,000/- and in case of default of payment of fine to undergo additional one month imprisonment.
15. Being dissatisfied with the conviction and sentence, both the accused-appellants have challenged their conviction and sentence before this Court by way of present appeal.

16. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned A.G.A. for the State.
17.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that there is no direct evidence against the accused-appellants with respect to setting ablaze the deceased.

Learned counsel next argued that prior to the alleged incident no report or complaint whatsoever was lodged against the accused-appellants and, therefore, the judgement and order of conviction suffers from material illegality and irregularity, thus the findings returned by the trial Court is perverse, illegal and the accused-appellants are liable to be acquitted.

18. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has submitted that there is brutality in causing death and it is a dowry death which has occurred within two and half years of marriage, therefore, there is no illegality or perversity in the judgment and order of conviction passed by the learned trial court, thus, the present appeal is liable to be dismissed.
19. Heard learned counsel for the parties and we have gone through the judgment and order of the trial court and also perused the lower court records.
20. In the facts of the case, we find that the deceased (wife) has died on account of burn injuries caused to her at her matrimonial house.
Her death is thus unnatural.
She has otherwise died well within seven years of her marriage.
The testimony of P.W.1 and P.W.3 clearly shows that there was demand of dowry by the accused-husband of a motorcycle which continued till soon before the death of the deceased.
In such circumstances, necessary ingredients of an offence under Section 304-B I.P.C. are clearly made out against the accused-husband/ appellant.
21. So far as the mother-in-law of the deceased, Smt. Urmila is concerned, she is a widow elderly lady.
There is no specific allegation of demand of dowry as against her.
The allegations regarding demand of dowry are otherwise omnibus and vague as against her.

No specific role is assigned to her Smt. Urmila And Another vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75150811/
4 in commissioning of the offence, either.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such circumstances, the mother-in-law of the deceased cannot be held liable for the offence under Section 304-B I.P.C.
No reasons are otherwise furnished in the judgment of conviction passed against her to hold her guilty.
Since prosecution has not succeeded in establishing guilt of accused, mother-in-law, under Section 304-B I.P.C. as such her conviction and sentence cannot be sustained.
22. Coming to the question of sentence, we find that the trial court has awarded life sentence to the accused appellant-Dharmendra under Section 304-B I.P.C.

Punishment under Section 304-B I.P.C.
varies from 7 years to life.
When the court proceeds to award maximum permissible sentence for an offence, it is the cardinal principle of law that reasons have to be given for awarding such maximum punishment.
We do not find any such reasons to have been disclosed by the trial court.
We otherwise find that there are no circumstances, which may justify awarding of extreme punishment to the accused appellant-Dharmendra in the facts of the present case.
Considering the evidence in its entirety, we are of the view that punishment of life under Section 304-B I.P.C. to the accused-appellant, Dharmendra, is not warranted.

23. In Hem Chand Vs. State of Haryana, (1994) 6 SCC 727, the Supreme Court has observed that though punishment under Section 304-B I.P.C. varies from 7 years to life but award of extreme punishment should not be as a matter of course and must be awarded in rare cases.

entities.text: Hem Chand Vs. State of Haryana, (1994) 6 SCC 727
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In para 7 and 8,
the Supreme Court observed as under:-
"7. Now coming to the question of sentence, it can be seen that Section 304-B IPC lays down that:
"Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life."
The point for consideration is whether the extreme punishment of imprisonment for life is warranted in the instant case.

A reading of Section 304-B IPC would show that when a question arises whether a person has committed the offence of dowry death of a woman what all that is necessary is it should be shown that soon before her unnatural death, which took place within seven years of the marriage, the deceased had been subjected, by such person, to cruelty or harassment for or in connection with demand for dowry.
If that is shown then the court shall presume that such a person has caused the dowry death.

It can therefore be seen that irrespective of the fact whether such person is directly responsible for the death of the deceased or not by virtue of the presumption,
he is deemed to have committed the dowry death if there were such cruelty or harassment and that if the unnatural death has occurred within seven years from the date of marriage.
Likewise there is a presumption under Section 113-B of the Evidence Act as to the dowry death.

It lays down that the court shall presume that the person who has subjected the deceased wife to cruelty before her death caused the dowry death if it is shown that before her death, such woman had been subjected, by the accused, to cruelty or harassment in connection with any demand for dowry.
Practically this is the presumption that has been incorporated in Section 304-B IPC also.

It can therefore be seen that irrespective of the fact whether the accused has any direct connection with the death or not, he shall Smt. Urmila And Another vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75150811/
5 be presumed to have committed the dowry death provided the other requirements mentioned above are satisfied.

sentences.text: In the instant case no doubt the prosecution has proved that the deceased died an unnatural death namely due to strangulation, but there is no direct evidence connecting the accused.
It is also important to note in this context that there is no charge under Section 302 IPC.
The trial court also noted that there were two sets of medical evidence on the file in respect of the death of the deceased.
Dr Usha Rani PW 6 and Dr Indu Lalit PW 7 gave one opinion.
According to them no injury was found on the dead body and that the same was highly decomposed.
On the other hand, Dr Dalbir Singh PW 13 who also examined the dead body and gave his opinion, deposed that he noticed some injuries at the time of re-post-mortem examination.
Therefore at the most it can be said that the prosecution proved that it was an unnatural death in which case also Section 304-B IPC would be attracted.
But this aspect has certainly to be taken into consideration in balancing the sentence to be awarded to the accused.

As a matter of fact, the trial court only found that the death was unnatural and the aspect of cruelty has been established and therefore the offences punishable under Sections 304-B and 201 IPC have been established.

The High Court in a very short judgment concluded that it was fully proved that the death of the deceased in her matrimonial home was a dowry death otherwise than in normal circumstances as a result of cruelty meted out to her and therefore an offence under Section 304-B IPC was made out.

Coming to the sentence the High Court pointed out that the accused-appellant was a police employee and instead of checking the crime, he himself indulged therein and precipitated in it and that bride-killing cases are on the increase and therefore a serious view has to be taken.
As mentioned above, Section 304-B IPC only raises presumption and lays down that minimum sentence should be seven years but it may extend to imprisonment for life.
Therefore awarding extreme punishment of imprisonment for life should be in rare cases and not in every case.
8. Hence, we are of the view that a sentence of 10 years' RI would meet the ends of justice.

We,
accordingly while confirming the conviction of the appellant under Section 304-B IPC, reduce the sentence of imprisonment for life to 10 years' RI.
The other conviction and sentence passed against the appellant are, however, confirmed.
In the result, the appeal is dismissed subject to the above modification of sentence."
24. In Kashmira Devi Vs. The State of Uttarakhand, AIR 2020 SC 652, the principle laid down in Hem Chand (supra) has been reiterated and the Court observed as under in para 24:-

entities.text: Kashmira Devi Vs. The State of Uttarakhand, AIR 2020 SC 652
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "24. Having arrived at the above conclusion the quantum of sentence requires consideration.
The High Court has awarded life imprisonment to the appellant on being convicted under Section 304-B IPC.
The minimum sentence provided is seven years but it may extend to imprisonment for life.

In fact, this Court in Hem Chand v.
State of Haryana [Hem Chand v. State of Haryana, (1994) 6 SCC 727 : 1995 SCC (Cri)

Hem Chand v.
State of Haryana [Hem Chand v. State of Haryana, (1994) 6 SCC 727 : 1995 SCC (Cri)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 36] has held that while imposing the sentence, awarding extreme punishment of imprisonment for life under Section 304-B IPC should be in rare cases and not in every case.

Though the mitigating factor noticed in the said case was different, in the instant case keeping in view the age of the appellant and also the contribution that would be required by her to the family, while husband is also aged and further taking into consideration all other circumstances, the sentence as awarded by the High Smt. Urmila And Another vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75150811/
6 Court to the appellant herein is liable to be modified."

Para 25 of the judgment in Kashmira Devi (supra) is, thus, reproduced hereinafter:-

"25. In the result, the following:
Order 25.1.

The conviction of the appellant recorded by the High Court under Section 304-B IPC and Section 498-A IPC through its judgment dated 29-6-2017 [State v.
Govind Singh, 2017 SCC OnLine Utt 1932] is upheld and affirmed.

State v.
Govind Singh, 2017 SCC OnLine Utt 1932
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Govind Singh, GA No. 42 of 2010, decided on 10-7-2017 (Utt)] is modified and the sentence of imprisonment for life is altered by ordering the appellant to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years which shall include the period of sentence already undergone by the appellant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The fine as imposed and the default sentence is sustained.
25.3. The appeal is allowed in part, in the above terms.
25.4. The parties to bear their own costs."
26. The accused-appellant, Dharmendra, has been taken in custody on 14.11.2014 and has remained in jail ever since then.
The actual period of incarceration undergone by him is about 4 years 9 months and with remission the incarceration period is almost 11 years.
We are of the considered view that the sentence awarded to him under Section 304-B I.P.C. be modified to the sentence already undergone by him.
The fine and the default sentence is maintained.

The appellant-Dharmendra is set to liberty on the sentence already undergone, subject to observance of Section 437A Cr.P.C.,
provided he is not wanted in any other case.
Consequently, present criminal appeal on behalf of accused-appellant, Dharmendra, succeeds and is allowed in part, to that extent.
27. For the reasons recorded above, the present criminal appeal on behalf of accused-appellant, Smt. Urmila, succeeds and is allowed.

The judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 09.12.2019 passed in Session Trial No. 151 of 2015,
arising out of Case Crime No. 315 of 2014, under Sections 498A, 304-B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kampil, District Farrukhabad,
against the accused-appellant, Smt. Urmila is set aside.
Consequently, she be released forthwith if not required in any other offence.
28. The trial Court record along with the copy of this Judgement and order be transmitted to the court concerned forthwith.
